-- All timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC strings. JSON columns are TEXT.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS admin_users (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
  role TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'admin',
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  last_login_at TEXT
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_admin_users_email ON admin_users(email);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  token_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
  csrf_token TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  expires_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  last_seen_at TEXT,
  ip TEXT,
  user_agent TEXT

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sessions_token ON sessions(token_hash);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sessions_expires ON sessions(expires_at);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS provider_instances (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  type TEXT NOT NULL,
  enabled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  base_url TEXT,
  timeout_ms INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 12000,
  max_concurrency INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 4,
  priority INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 100,
  weight INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 100,
  max_retries INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,

  daily_quota INTEGER,
  key_strategy TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'round_robin',

  config_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at TEXT NOT NULL

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_provider_instances_name ON provider_instances(name);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_provider_instances_type ON provider_instances(type);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS api_keys (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  provider_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES provider_instances(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  label TEXT NOT NULL,

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_api_keys_provider ON api_keys(provider_id);

--
-- `search_config_json` holds the per-instance search parameters (targetResults,

migrations.name: 0004_search_cache.sql
migrations.sql:
-- Persistent search cache (v0.1.7).
--
-- Replaces the in-memory Map that vanished on every restart. The cache lives in
-- the same SQLite database as everything else, so a Docker volume, a systemd
-- restart or a Windows reboot all keep it — and so the existing backup and
-- upgrade paths cover it without extra work.
--
-- `cache_key` is a SHA-256 of the request fingerprint, never the query text: a
-- raw query as a primary key turns the table into a readable search history and
-- makes long queries expensive to index.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "search_cache" (
  "cache_key" text PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
  "response_json" text NOT NULL,
  "status" text NOT NULL,
  "mode" text NOT NULL,
  "created_at" text NOT NULL,
  "expires_at" text NOT NULL,
  "last_accessed_at" text NOT NULL,
  -- UTF-8 byte length of `response_json`, not the JS string length.
  "size_bytes" integer NOT NULL,
  "hit_count" integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);
--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "idx_search_cache_expires"
  ON "search_cache" ("expires_at");
--> statement-breakpoint
-- LRU eviction sorts by this column, so it must be indexed.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "idx_search_cache_accessed"
  ON "search_cache" ("last_accessed_at");
--> statement-breakpoint

-- Hourly counters. Bounded by construction (one row per hour), so the 24-hour
-- hit rate stays a cheap query and a quiet instance can say "no data yet"
-- instead of inventing a percentage from one request.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "search_cache_metrics" (
  "bucket" text PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
  "hits" integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  "misses" integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  "expired_removed" integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  "evicted" integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  "updated_at" text NOT NULL
);
--> statement-breakpoint

-- Bookkeeping that must survive a restart: last sweep time, lifetime totals.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "search_cache_state" (
  "key" text PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
  "value" text NOT NULL,
  "updated_at" text NOT NULL
);

migrations.name: 0005_provider_health_center.sql
migrations.sql:
-- Provider health management centre (v0.1.7).
--
-- Two things live here, and neither duplicates the append-only probe log in
-- `provider_health_checks`:
--
--  1. `provider_probe_state` — the *scheduler's* bookkeeping for one provider:
--     whether automatic probing is on, how many consecutive failures it has,
--     how far the exponential backoff has gone, and when the next attempt is
--     due. Keeping it out of `provider_health_checks` means a schedule change
--     never rewrites history.
--
--  2. `health_probe_budget` — a durable ledger of probe spend, one row per UTC
--     day and probe kind. Counting rows in the probe log would be a
--     read-then-act race: two concurrent probes both see "19 used" and both
--     spend. The ledger is decremented by a conditional UPDATE, so the limit
--     holds under concurrency.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "provider_probe_state" (
  "provider_id" text PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL
    REFERENCES "provider_instances"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- Per-provider switch. The global switch still gates everything: this can
  -- only turn a provider *off* within an enabled schedule.
  "auto_probe_enabled" integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  "consecutive_failures" integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  "backoff_level" integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  "next_probe_at" text,
  -- Manual reset: probe rows older than this no longer determine the status,
  -- but they stay in the log for audit.
  "reset_at" text,
  "updated_at" text NOT NULL
);
--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "idx_probe_state_next"
  ON "provider_probe_state" ("next_probe_at");
--> statement-breakpoint

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "health_probe_budget" (
  -- UTC date, YYYY-MM-DD. The boundary is documented in docs/provider-health.md.
  "day" text NOT NULL,
  "kind" text NOT NULL,
  "used" integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  "updated_at" text NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY ("day", "kind")
);

migrations.name: 0006_search_quality.sql
migrations.sql:
-- Search quality evaluation lab (v0.1.8).
--
-- Five tables, deliberately separated by lifetime:
--
--  1. `quality_datasets` / `quality_queries` / `quality_judgments` are the
--     *input*: a versioned qrel set. Freezing a dataset bumps its version and
--     makes it read-only, so a score produced yesterday stays interpretable.
--
--  2. `quality_runs` is one experiment's context: dataset version, code commit,
--     engine version, fusion parameters and the budget it was allowed to spend.
--
--  3. `quality_snapshots` is the *raw per-provider result list* of one run. It
--     is what makes a comparison fair: two fusion strategies are re-ranked from
--     the same snapshot instead of from two different network moments.
--
--  4. `quality_run_results` is the per-query ranked list plus its metrics, so a
--     regression can be traced to a specific query and document rather than to
--     an average.
--
-- No table stores a credential, and no table references `search_tasks`: an
-- evaluation is not a user search, and must not appear in success-rate
-- statistics or be readable from another token's task list.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "quality_datasets" (
  "id" text PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
  "name" text NOT NULL,
  "description" text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  "language" text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'zh',
  -- Monotonic; bumped by freeze. A run records the version it used.
  "version" integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  "status" text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft',
  -- manual | imported | synthetic_fixture. Decides what a score may be called.
  "origin" text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'manual',
  -- 1 only when the qrels are exhaustive for this query set: recall is N/A
  -- otherwise, never computed from a partial ground truth.
  "judgments_complete" integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  "created_at" text NOT NULL,
  "updated_at" text NOT NULL,
  "frozen_at" text
);
--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "idx_quality_datasets_status"
  ON "quality_datasets" ("status");
--> statement-breakpoint

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "quality_queries" (
  "id" text PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
  "dataset_id" text NOT NULL
    REFERENCES "quality_datasets"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE,
  "query" text NOT NULL,
  "category" text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'general',
  "language" text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'zh',
  "intent" text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  "notes" text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  "created_at" text NOT NULL
);
--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "idx_quality_queries_dataset"
  ON "quality_queries" ("dataset_id");
--> statement-breakpoint

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "quality_judgments" (
  "id" text PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
  "dataset_id" text NOT NULL
    REFERENCES "quality_datasets"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE,
  "query_id" text NOT NULL
    REFERENCES "quality_queries"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- Normalized document identity (normalizeUrl). Never a list position: a
  -- position changes between runs, the document does not.
  "document_id" text NOT NULL,
  -- 0 off-topic, 1 mentions the topic, 2 answers part, 3 answers the intent.
  "relevance" integer NOT NULL,
  "assessor" text NOT NULL,
  -- human | machine_generated | synthetic_fixture. Only `human` is truth.
  "source" text NOT NULL,
  "notes" text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  "created_at" text NOT NULL,
  "updated_at" text NOT NULL
);
--> statement-breakpoint
-- One grade per document per query. A second judgment replaces the first, which
-- keeps a re-assessment from silently doubling the qrel set.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "idx_quality_judgments_document"
  ON "quality_judgments" ("query_id", "document_id");
--> statement-breakpoint

  ON "quality_judgments" ("dataset_id");
--> statement-breakpoint

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "quality_runs" (
  "id" text PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
  "dataset_id" text NOT NULL,
  -- Copied at start: editing the dataset later must not reinterpret this run.
  "dataset_version" integer NOT NULL,
  "dataset_origin" text NOT NULL,
  "name" text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  "notes" text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  -- offline | live. Offline never leaves the process.
  "mode" text NOT NULL,
  "fusion_strategy" text NOT NULL,
  "fusion_json" text NOT NULL,

  -- comparison that re-derives the cutoff from a default would silently compare

  "cutoff_value" integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 10,

  "snapshot_run_id" text,

  "query_count" integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  "error_json" text,
  "metrics_json" text,
  "actor" text,
  "started_at" text NOT NULL,
  "finished_at" text,

-- Quality lab provenance and query categories (v0.1.10).
--
-- Additive only: every statement is an ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN with a default
-- where a value is required. A database written by v0.1.9 keeps every row it
-- already had, and the new columns read as "not recorded" rather than as an
-- invented value:
--
--   * `provider_ids_json` / `provider_fingerprint` / `model_fingerprint` /
--     `qrels_fingerprint` stay NULL on old runs. Filling them from the *current*
--     configuration would describe a run that never happened.
--   * `per_provider_limit` / `request_timeout_ms` stay NULL: v0.1.9 used an
--     implicit limit and the engine default, and neither is recoverable.
--   * `failure_reason` distinguishes a run that failed at persistence from one
--     that failed upstream. Old failures keep NULL and are reported as unknown.
--   * `persisted_query_count` / `partial` default to 0: an old run stored
--     complete results by construction.
--
-- `extra_categories` is a JSON array of the secondary category labels. The
-- primary label stays in `category`, so an old client that never sends extra
-- labels is still valid and reads back as a single-category query.

ALTER TABLE "quality_queries"
  ADD COLUMN "extra_categories" text NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]';

-- anonymous bucket was polluted by the v0.1.10 seed bug, so only exact anonymous

WITH "classified" AS (
  SELECT
    "billing"."budget_day" AS "day",
    "billing"."budget_kind" AS "budget_kind",
    "billing"."classification" AS "classification",
    count(*) AS "used"
  FROM "provider_health_billing" AS "billing"
  WHERE "billing"."spent" = 1
  GROUP BY "day", "budget_kind", "classification"
)

SET

    WHEN 'search' THEN max("used", coalesce((
      SELECT sum("classified"."used")
      FROM "classified"
      WHERE "classified"."day" = "health_probe_budget"."day"
        AND "classified"."budget_kind" = 'search'
    ), 0))
    WHEN 'connect' THEN max("used", coalesce((
      SELECT sum("classified"."used")
      FROM "classified"
      WHERE "classified"."day" = "health_probe_budget"."day"
        AND "classified"."budget_kind" = 'connect'
    ), 0))
    WHEN 'search_anonymous' THEN coalesce((

      FROM "classified"
      WHERE "classified"."day" = "health_probe_budget"."day"
        AND "classified"."budget_kind" = 'search_anonymous'
        AND "classified"."classification" = 'exact'
    ), 0)
    ELSE "used"
  END,
  "updated_at" = strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')
WHERE "kind" IN ('search', 'connect', 'search_anonymous')
